comment: Had 301; by far the best person I could think to teach me CPU circuitry. The grading here is a bit strange: there's three categories of assignments, all graded pass/fail. Your grade depends on how many of these assignments you complete, and there's not many. You could be in for some end-of-semester cleanup if you're not careful. Still reccommended!

Took her CS301 and she is genuinely a great professor who can teach very well. She explains things in accessible, understandable terms and uses a lot of examples. She is also very helpful when you are struggling to do something and she does not make you feel dumb when you don't get something.

Though clearly a good teacher, Dr. Dollak gives loads of homework. The digital textbook,zylabs, could take hours which dumps alot of text and code to decipher before coding. Sometimes it expects us to know things we havent been taught. And the labs were very lengthy, hard and stressful after a few weeks. Difficult class. Fair grader and accessible.

Well-paced course, labs were well structured based on the content of the class. Passionate about computer science, super helpful in office hours as well as during class if you have questions. Highly recommend, easy course and wonderful woman.

Once you get past the logic of programming, the course is engaging. Dr. Dollak has fun presentations and you can tell that she is passionate about CS. In class exercises check for understanding. Outside of class, the programming assignments are time-consuming but I never felt unprepared for them. Overall great prof. even for a hard topic to intro.

Very passionate about the subject. Lectures were tedious and people barely participated in the group problems. The labs sometimes took a lot more than two hours. She did not grade most of the labs until the last week of school (and into finals week) so it was hard to gauge how you were doing. Overall a good class for learning Python basics though.

The class is pretty straightforward/well paced. Dr. Dollak cares about her students and is super knowledgeable. Labs can be challenging but have clear expectations and relevance to the course material (and are kinda satisfying). Definitely use office hours if you feel stuck/confused. Feel like I built a good foundation for CS.

She's passionate about the subject, extremely smart, cares about improving her teaching style, and facilitates hands-on activities. Her labs can be tricky, but she's helpful during office hours. I hadn't done any coding whatsoever before taking this course, but I enjoyed her class very much (even when it made me want to tear my hair out).
